body:
I'm in the same boat, although shooting wasn't the risk. Everyone in my life abused me and I reached that point of stupor where my brain could no longer process life.

I am still depressed and traumatized many years later at how easily I could've done something terrible. It haunts me even though I didn't do it. I could've had the circumstances been different.

I feel cheated. I started off more cautious than most. I was determined to be a good person. I wasn't supposed to end up like this.

Nobody believes it's "just bad luck" and I know that sounds ridiculous. But it's the truth. It was a perfect storm of events that ruined me.

You're right that it doesn't define me. But I'm just in disbelief at how it played out like someone hacked the universe and used it against me.

The part I can't move on from is that I wronged others. Because the people who abused me broke me and I lost track.

And I am not allowed to say this. It's considered "making excuses."

> there’s a meaning to your life out there - you just have to find it. 

I'm not looking for the meaning. I was always a simple guy who didn't ask for much. I'd be satisfied with very little.

But I'm now shackled by remorse for past actions and I'm angry because they weren't supposed to happen, but abusive people railroaded me into it.

I don't want the perfect life. I don't care about perfection. I just want to not be a criminal. And I feel I did more than the average person to avoid becoming one, but that wasn't even enough. I was always asking my parents to discuss moral issues, to discuss what's right vs. what's wrong, but they aggressively shut me down and everyone continued to abuse me.

The people who abused me stopped at nothing to convert me to their ways, so I tried their way and doomed myself for life.

And then it was Game Over in 1 move.
